title: Package the first Codex hooks Adapter

requirement.summary: Connect Codex lifecycle hooks to the existing vendor-neutral AgentGov foreground coordinator without collecting prompts, source, tool payloads, transcripts, or assistant messages.

objective.rationale: The generic JSONL process transport is implemented, but ordinary Codex use still needs a reviewed project hook configuration and a host-specific mapper that invokes the same vendor-neutral coordinator automatically.

goal: Add a packaged Codex hook Adapter for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, and Stop plus a create-missing-only project hook integration preview and explicit apply path.
non_goals: Do not parse task scope, approval, semantic acceptance, or authority from raw prompt or assistant text.

Do not persist or forward prompt, source, tool_input, tool_response, transcript_path, last_assistant_message, credentials, model, or absolute host paths from Codex hook input into AgentGov events or hook output.
Do not add a daemon, App Server dependency, network request, automatic upload, plugin installation, or hidden hook trust bypass.
Do not merge with or overwrite an existing .codex/hooks.json file.
Do not grant scope expansion, exception, commit, push, merge, release, publication, deployment, or external-system authority.
Do not commit, push, tag, release, publish, install the generated hooks in this repository, or modify a consumer repository.
acceptance_signals: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, and Stop map deterministically to repository.activated, task.requested, implementation.changed, and completion.requested without vendor fields entering Core contracts.
The Adapter validates the hook event, session/turn identity, repository binding, and supported event-specific facts while explicitly discarding sensitive Codex payload fields.

A missing active task reaches Codex as bounded additional context rather than inferred task admission; material scope and completion failures reach Codex without claiming a completed side-effect was undone.
Stop continuation is bounded by stop_hook_active so the Adapter cannot create an infinite completion loop.
The managed .codex/hooks.json preview is deterministic, create-missing-only, preserves existing files, requires exact interactive confirmation to write, and leaves Codex hook trust to the user.
The existing generic JSONL transport, single-cycle CLI, GitHub Actions integration, and headless lifecycle fixtures remain compatible.
Focused tests, the complete supported-Python suite, task/scope/repository checks, schema parsing, packaging assertions, and diff checks pass.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_codex_hooks tests.test_coding_agent_transport tests.test_foreground_coordinator tests.test_cli -v

items: Hook input includes raw prompt, tool, transcript, and assistant fields that must never enter AgentGov events or output.
PostToolUse occurs after side effects and must not claim that a scope finding undid or prevented the tool action.
A Stop continuation can loop unless repeat invocation is explicitly bounded.
An existing project hook configuration could contain user policy that must not be overwritten or silently merged.
Project hooks require Codex trust review and may be disabled by user or managed configuration.

stop_conditions: Stop if current official Codex documentation does not establish the required hook events or structured output behavior.
Stop if implementation requires retaining prompt, source, tool payload, transcript, assistant message, credential, or absolute path data.
Stop if hook configuration must bypass Codex trust review, overwrite existing config, become governance authority, or run as a hidden daemon.
Stop if PostToolUse would be described as undoing a completed side effect or a coding-agent event could self-approve scope or semantic completion.
Stop before any Git write, plugin install, hook installation in this repository, release, consumer mutation, or external-system write.

decision.rationale: The Codex hooks Adapter implementation and validation are complete. The task is paused for routing hygiene while the user-authorized development completion communication guidance is added; this does not claim commit, release, publication, or external acceptance.
